clue.text: Stands naked holding up end of wedding tackle

indicators.note: in a down entry, what holds something up sits beneath it, so this piece goes below the other
something naked has had its outer covering stripped away, so the word loses its outside letters
the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: last letter of wedding
stands, as in tolerates, is bears

explanation.surface: A crude joke about a naked man at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: BEARS without its outer letters leaves EAR; in a down light it holds up G by sitting under it, giving GEAR. The wedding tackle of the surface is a cheeky euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear and tackle are both general words for the equipment needed for an activity, such as fishing kit.

clue.text: 22 scores having great influence but not well-liked to begin with

indicators.note: but not asks for the following item to be left out of the longer word

parts.note: a weighty matter carries great influence

indicators.note: what comes to begin with in a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: first letter of well-liked

explanation.surface: A sporting statistic about an influential but unpopular figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 22 is FOUR, so 22 scores means four times twenty. WEIGHTY loses its W.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so four lots of twenty make the number eighty.

clue.text: Embellish contents of more books about celebrity

indicators.note: about means going around, so the earlier letters surround the next item
the contents of a word are its inner letters, without the first and last

parts.note: the inside letters of more
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
a celebrity is a big name

explanation.surface: Someone padding out the contents of yet more books about a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Contents of more means only its inside letters. The first pair of pieces is split around the third, so about is placing, not a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To ornament something is to decorate or adorn it, the same as embellishing it.

clue.text: Minister upset church before interrupting bishop

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another item

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to means before, as in ten to six

explanation.surface: A clergyman cross with the church and the bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Before is the to of ten to six, a sense solvers often miss; Right Reverend is how bishops are styled.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest, a minister of religion in charge of a parish.

clue.text: Beat up apprentice overtaking learner driver?

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to flog is to beat

indicators.note: overtaking here means taking over and enclosing the next item

parts.note: a cub is a novice or apprentice, as in cub reporter
L is the learner sign

explanation.surface: A road-rage scene: someone beating up an apprentice who overtook a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: Driver is not a motorist but the definition, with a question mark because it is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is a particular kind of golf club, used for long shots from the tee.

clue.text: Draw tea service from a different perspective

indicators.note: seen from a different perspective, the letters are viewed in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist sketching a tea set from a new angle.
explanation.walkthrough: Draw looks like sketching, but it is the old sense of disembowelling, as in hanged, drawn and quartered.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a carcass or a traitor is to remove the entrails, which is to eviscerate.

clue.text: Never about to stop working, though not against wanting more

indicators.note: not asks for the following item to be left out of the word
about means going around, so the first word surrounds the next item

parts.note: taken as written
a machine that dies stops working
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: Someone who will never retire, but not because they oppose wanting more.
explanation.walkthrough: Though not against reads like part of the story, but it tells you to drop the versus letter from the first word once it has wrapped around the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Needier is the comparative of needy, describing someone in greater want or lacking more.

clue.text: Number 10 tripled it in error

indicators.note: letters set down in error are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 10 across is a compass direction, abbreviated NE, written three times
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sum done wrongly: someone tripled ten and got it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 looks like the number ten, but it points to 10 across, NORTHEAST, whose abbreviation NE is used three times.
explanation.definitionFit: Nineteen is a whole number, so number defines it in the general sense of a numeral.

clue.text: Delegate's cycling changed over time

indicators.note: cycling moves the front letter round to the back, like a wheel turning

parts.note: to devolve power is to delegate it

explanation.surface: A conference delegate who cycles in each morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the front of DEVOLVE moves to the end. The 's is short for is, linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that evolved developed gradually, altering its form across a long period.

clue.text: Man's expected to embrace daughter

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: something due is expected
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A father is expected to hug his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: DU(D)E; the 's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude is informal slang, chiefly American, for a man or a guy.

clue.text: Direction of new articles written in alternative way

indicators.note: words written in something are placed inside it

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
or introduces an alternative
the and a are the definite and indefinite articles
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: Editorial guidance that new articles be written in a different style.
explanation.walkthrough: N, then THE and A written in OR and ST: N + OR(THEA)ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Northeast is a compass point, one of the bearings or directions between north and east.

clue.text: Stuck together once law enforcement agent's arrested us

indicators.note: someone arrested is held, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a fed is American slang for an FBI agent
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people handcuffed together after an FBI agent arrested them.
explanation.walkthrough: FE(US)D; the 's stands for has.
explanation.definitionFit: Fused means joined or welded into one, as melted metals bond when they cool.

clue.text: Creep about idly, unevenly and erratically

indicators.note: moving erratically means going in no fixed order, so the letters are jumbled
unevenly means taking the odd-numbered letters only, skipping the even ones

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters of about idly

explanation.surface: Someone creeping around lazily and unsteadily.
explanation.walkthrough: Creep looks like a verb of moving slowly, matching the surface, but it is a noun for a sycophant.
explanation.definitionFit: A creep, in the sense of a sycophant, is a toady who flatters superiors to win favour.

clue.text: Fuss about timeless novel beginning to alienate fan

indicators.note: timeless means without time, whose abbreviation is dropped from the word
a fuss about something comes attached to it, so these pieces simply join up
the beginning of a word is its first letter alone

parts.note: first letter of alienate
a novel is a work of fiction
ado is fuss, as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: A fuss over a novel whose opening puts off its fans.
explanation.walkthrough: FICTION loses T (time). A leads, then FICION, then ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: An aficionado is an enthusiast or devotee who knows a lot about a hobby, which is a fan.

clue.text: Registered being on board submarine?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: signed up, entered on a list of members
second meaning, playful: put into a sub, a long bread roll, so in-rolled

explanation.walkthrough: Submarine is not a boat but a sub sandwich, a long roll; something on board one has been put in a roll.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to put a name on the roll or register, so someone enrolled has been registered.

clue.text: British rugby supporter follows opening of tournament without any feeling

indicators.note: follows places the supporter after the piece just before it

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for British
RU is rugby union

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of tournament
an ally supports you

explanation.surface: A British rugby fan arriving at the start of a tournament, apparently numb.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union is routinely shortened in crosswords; supporter is a friend on your side, not a fan in the stands.
explanation.definitionFit: To act brutally is to act savagely and pitilessly, showing no compassion for the victim.

clue.text: European bishop's retreat showcasing paintings collected by wealthy writer originally

indicators.note: something collected by another is gathered inside it

parts.note: EUR is an abbreviation for European

indicators.note: a showcase holds things on display, so one word encloses the next

parts.note: rich means wealthy
paintings are art
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a lair is a hideaway or retreat

explanation.surface: A European bishop's country retreat displaying artworks bought by a rich patron.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: paintings sit in wealthy, and both sit within European after its first letter. Eric Arthur Blair was George Orwell's real name, hence originally.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Arthur Blair, the name the writer was born with.

clue.text: Prove a Bachelor of Arts may be at a premium

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could become something else once rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
BA is the degree abbreviation

explanation.surface: A graduate wondering whether the degree proves worth its high price.
explanation.definitionFit: Shares above par sell for more than their face value, which is the financial sense of a premium.

clue.text: Rise and fall of Latin garnering excessive coverage

indicators.note: garnering means gathering in, so one item ends up surrounded
coverage is a covering laid around something, enclosing it

parts.note: undue means excessive
LAT is the abbreviation for Latin

explanation.surface: A report on the decline of Latin getting too much press attention.
explanation.walkthrough: Latin gets excessive coverage: UNDU(LAT)E.
explanation.definitionFit: To undulate is to move in waves, going up and down repeatedly like a swell on the sea.

clue.text: Honour-bound men went outside and disbanded union

indicators.note: bound means tied round, so the first item encloses the next

parts.note: went is a euphemism for died, as in passed away

indicators.note: going outside something means surrounding it

parts.note: the VC, Victoria Cross, is Britain's highest gallantry award
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Soldiers bound by honour who left and broke up their trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the honour binds the men, and went wraps around both. Union is marriage here, not a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorced couple has legally dissolved the union of marriage, ending it as a partnership.

clue.text: Rogue has hardly any support when it's time to go home

indicators.note: in a down entry, a support sits underneath, so the second piece goes below the first

parts.note: a cur is a scoundrel
few means hardly any

explanation.surface: A scoundrel with few backers when the night ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is a fixed hour after which people must be indoors, often imposed on teenagers or by martial law.

clue.text: Fleece is beginning to conserve warmth

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is just its first letter

parts.note: first letter of conserve
heat is warmth

explanation.surface: A fleece jacket is starting to keep you warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleece looks like the garment, but it is the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them out of money, which is to cheat them.

clue.text: Force railway to provide platform for school

indicators.note: in a down entry, a platform sits beneath what it carries, so this piece goes underneath

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive, a British state secondary school
EL is an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A railway forced to build a station platform for a school.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel is to oblige someone, forcing them to act against their will.

clue.text: Cardinal heeded warning

indicators.note: heeded suggests what was heard, so the word goes by its sound

parts.note: fore is the warning a golfer calls

explanation.surface: A cardinal of the church took notice of a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinal is not a churchman but a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal numbers are the counting numbers one, two, three and so on, which include this one.

clue.text: Cat scratching sleeve of jumper

indicators.note: the sleeve is the outer covering, and scratching it off removes the outside letters

parts.note: one who pounces is a jumper

explanation.surface: A cat clawing at the sleeve of a woollen jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper looks like the British word for a sweater, but it is one who jumps; POUNCER loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asian mountains.

clue.text: Part One providing artist with inspiration for example

parts.note: an actor's part is a role
an artist's sitter inspires the work

explanation.surface: An actor's role is to be an artist's muse.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose conduct sets an example that others copy.

clue.text: Board of Trade

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a plank of pine or fir timber
second meaning: to do business, buy and sell

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the name of a British government body, the Board of Trade, but splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is softwood timber cut into planks, and to deal in goods is to trade them.

clue.text: One jailed by court after gunmen spread out

indicators.note: after places this piece behind the one that comes before

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

indicators.note: someone jailed by another is held inside, so one item is enclosed

parts.note: to court someone is to date them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A prisoner jailed by a court after a gang of gunmen scattered.
explanation.walkthrough: RA + D(I)ATE. Court is the verb of romance, not a law court.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to extend outwards from a centre in all directions, as spokes or rays do.

clue.text: These people must take blame for ill treatment

indicators.note: taking something in holds it within, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: they means these people
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Those responsible must accept blame for mistreating someone.
explanation.walkthrough: THE(RAP)Y. Ill treatment reads as abuse, but it means treatment for the ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is medical or psychological care given to sick people to heal them.
